title: CTS Parables of the Bible — Unit 7: The Sower

blocks.en: 🌾 Parables of the Bible — Unit 7: The Sower
blocks.es_reference: 🌾 Las Parábolas de la Biblia — Unidad 7: El Sembrador

blocks.en: Professor: Dr. Wayne Cook | Director: Dr. Ted Rogers
blocks.es_reference: Profesor: Dr. Wayne Cook | Director: Dr. Ted Rogers

blocks.en: "Listen! Behold, a sower went out to sow." — Mark 4:3 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "Oíd: He aquí, el sembrador salió a sembrar." — Marcos 4:3 (RVG)

blocks.en: "Listen! Behold, a sower went out to sow" (Mark 4:3).
blocks.es_reference: "Oíd: He aquí, el sembrador salió a sembrar" (Marcos 4:3).

blocks.en: Orientation
blocks.es_reference: Orientación

blocks.en: With this unit we cross from the prophets to the parables of Jesus, and we begin where Jesus Himself seems to have begun. When the disciples asked Him about the parable of the sower, He answered, "Do you not understand this parable? How then will you understand all the parables?" (Mark 4:13). This is the parable that teaches us how to hear every other parable. It is about hearing itself.
blocks.es_reference: Con esta unidad pasamos de los profetas a las parábolas de Jesús, y comenzamos donde Jesús mismo parece haber comenzado. Cuando los discípulos le preguntaron por la parábola del sembrador, respondió: "¿No sabéis esta parábola? ¿Cómo, pues, entenderéis todas las parábolas?" (Marcos 4:13). Esta es la parábola que nos enseña a oír todas las demás. Trata del oír mismo.

blocks.en: Mark 4 sets the scene. So great a crowd gathered by the Sea of Galilee that Jesus got into a boat and sat in it, and the whole multitude stood on the shore (Mark 4:1). The fields He described were probably visible on the hillsides behind them. "Listen!" He began. "Behold, a sower went out to sow" (4:3). In this unit we study the parable of the sower and Jesus' explanation of it, and then two short parables that follow it in Mark 4: the lamp and the measure, and the seed that grows by itself. Together they teach how the word of God is received, how it must be heard, and how it grows.
blocks.es_reference: Marcos 4 prepara la escena. Se reunió alrededor de Él tanta gente junto al mar de Galilea que Jesús entró en una barca y se sentó en ella, y toda la multitud estaba en tierra junto al mar (Marcos 4:1). Probablemente los campos que describía se veían en las laderas detrás de ellos. "Oíd", comenzó. "He aquí, el sembrador salió a sembrar" (4:3). En esta unidad estudiamos la parábola del sembrador y la explicación de Jesús, y luego dos parábolas breves que la siguen en Marcos 4: la lámpara y la medida, y la semilla que crece por sí sola. Juntas enseñan cómo se recibe la palabra de Dios, cómo debe oírse y cómo crece.

blocks.en: I. The Soils: How People Receive the Word (Mark 4:1–20)
blocks.es_reference: I. Los terrenos: cómo reciben las personas la palabra (Marcos 4:1–20)

blocks.en: "A parable has been described as an earthly story with a heavenly meaning." I began a Baptism Sunday sermon with those words in 1981, and they fit this parable perfectly. Jesus paints a picture of a farmer in Palestine. He reaches into the bag at his waist, grabs a handful of seed, and broadcasts it across his field. Some scholars believe farmers in Jesus' day often sowed first and plowed the seed in afterward, which would explain why seed fell in so many kinds of ground. Jesus Himself explains the story: "The sower sows the word" (Mark 4:14). In this parable the emphasis is not on the sower, nor on the seed. It is on the soils. When people hear about Jesus, four things can happen.
blocks.es_reference: "Se ha dicho que una parábola es una historia terrenal con un significado celestial." Comencé un sermón de domingo de bautismos con esas palabras en 1981, y encajan perfectamente con esta parábola. Jesús pinta el cuadro de un agricultor en Palestina. Mete la mano en la bolsa que lleva en la cintura, toma un puñado de semilla y la esparce a voleo por su campo. Algunos eruditos creen que en los días de Jesús los agricultores a menudo sembraban primero y araban después para enterrar la semilla, lo cual explicaría por qué la semilla caía en tantas clases de terreno. Jesús mismo explica la historia: "El sembrador es el que siembra la palabra" (Marcos 4:14). En esta parábola el énfasis no está en el sembrador ni en la semilla. Está en los terrenos. Cuando las personas oyen de Jesús, pueden suceder cuatro cosas.

blocks.en: 1. Some people refuse to hear. In Palestine the fields were divided into long, narrow strips. There were no fences, so narrow footpaths ran between them, and people walked them until they were as hard as cement. Seed that fell there could not penetrate the surface, and the birds took it. Some people close their minds to the gospel. Some are indifferent: they are not hostile, they simply could not care less, the way some people feel about a sport that does not interest them. But life is very short, and eternity is very long. Others are hardened; they know that receiving Christ means sharing their lives with Him, and they will not let down the drawbridge. Jesus says that Satan comes immediately and takes away the word (4:15).
blocks.es_reference: 1. Algunos se niegan a oír. En Palestina los campos estaban divididos en franjas largas y angostas. No había cercas, así que entre ellos corrían senderos angostos, y la gente los caminaba hasta que quedaban duros como cemento. La semilla que caía allí no podía penetrar la superficie, y las aves se la comían. Algunas personas cierran la mente al evangelio. Algunas son indiferentes: no son hostiles, sencillamente no les importa, como algunos sienten acerca de un deporte que no les interesa. Pero la vida es muy corta, y la eternidad es muy larga. Otras están endurecidas; saben que recibir a Cristo significa compartir su vida con Él, y no quieren bajar el puente levadizo. Jesús dice que Satanás viene en seguida y quita la palabra (4:15).

blocks.en: 2. Some people have a shallow response. The rocky ground was not soil with stones in it. It was a thin skin of soil over a shelf of limestone. The seed sprang up quickly, but the roots could not go down, and when the sun beat down, the young plant withered. These are the ones who "immediately receive it with gladness; and they have no root in themselves, and so endure only for a time" (4:16–17). We have all heard of foxhole conversions. I once knew a young man who was an alcoholic and a compulsive gambler. His wife was about to leave him, and he had a religious experience. The next time I saw him he was still drinking, still gambling, and living with another woman. The first trouble he met destroyed his experience. Perhaps he tried to substitute enthusiasm for faith. There is a place for joy in the Christian life, but joy is a poor substitute for faith. When Paul met the risen Christ on the road to Damascus, he did not jump for joy; he spent three days in blindness, prayer, and fasting, considering what had happened to him (Acts 9:9).
blocks.es_reference: 2. Algunos tienen una respuesta superficial. Los pedregales no eran tierra con piedras. Eran una capa delgada de tierra sobre una losa de piedra caliza. La semilla brotaba pronto, pero las raíces no podían bajar, y cuando el sol calentaba, la plantita se secaba. Estos son los que "al momento la reciben con gozo; pero no tienen raíz en sí, sino que son de corta duración" (4:16–17). Todos hemos oído de las conversiones de trinchera. Una vez conocí a un joven que era alcohólico y jugador compulsivo. Su esposa estaba a punto de dejarlo, y él tuvo una experiencia religiosa. La siguiente vez que lo vi seguía bebiendo, seguía apostando y vivía con otra mujer. El primer problema que encontró destruyó su experiencia. Quizás trató de sustituir la fe con entusiasmo. Hay lugar para el gozo en la vida cristiana, pero el gozo es un pobre sustituto de la fe. Cuando Pablo se encontró con Cristo resucitado en el camino a Damasco, no saltó de gozo; pasó tres días ciego, orando y ayunando, considerando lo que le había sucedido (Hechos 9:9).

blocks.en: When I was teaching seminary, one of my students told me about the night he became a Christian. Several others made decisions at the same time, and some were so excited they were jumping up and down. For him, he said, it was more like, "Yeah, okay, I'll become a Christian." Many of those excited ones later fell away. But that quiet young man kept growing, and he ended up in seminary. The size of the first response does not predict the depth of the root.
blocks.es_reference: Cuando yo enseñaba en el seminario, uno de mis estudiantes me contó de la noche en que se hizo cristiano. Varios otros tomaron decisiones al mismo tiempo, y algunos estaban tan emocionados que saltaban de gozo. Para él, dijo, fue más bien algo como: "Bueno, está bien, me haré cristiano." Muchos de aquellos emocionados después se apartaron. Pero aquel joven callado siguió creciendo y terminó en el seminario. El tamaño de la primera respuesta no predice la profundidad de la raíz.

blocks.en: 3. Some people have divided hearts. The thorny ground may have belonged to a lazy farmer who, instead of pulling up the weeds, cut them down and burned them. The field looked clean, but the roots were still there. When the rains came, the thorns grew faster than the wheat and choked it. These are the ones in whom "the cares of this world, the deceitfulness of riches, and the desires for other things entering in choke the word" (4:19). One person says, "I will accept Christ, but I cannot stop drinking." Another says, "I like what Jesus says, but I will not give up my immoral conduct." The rich young ruler wanted eternal life, but he loved his money more, and he went away sad (Mark 10:17–22). God slowly moves to the back burner, and other loves crowd Him out.
blocks.es_reference: 3. Algunos tienen el corazón dividido. El terreno de espinos quizás pertenecía a un agricultor perezoso que, en lugar de arrancar la maleza, la cortó y la quemó. El campo se veía limpio, pero las raíces seguían allí. Cuando llegaron las lluvias, los espinos crecieron más rápido que el trigo y lo ahogaron. Estos son aquellos en quienes "los afanes de este siglo, y el engaño de las riquezas, y las codicias de otras cosas, entran y ahogan la palabra" (4:19). Una persona dice: "Aceptaré a Cristo, pero no puedo dejar de beber." Otra dice: "Me gusta lo que dice Jesús, pero no voy a dejar mi conducta inmoral." El joven rico quería la vida eterna, pero amaba más su dinero, y se fue triste (Marcos 10:17–22). Poco a poco Dios queda en segundo plano, y otros amores lo desplazan.

blocks.en: 4. Some people receive the word and bear fruit. Good soil is open, deep, and undivided. It receives the seed, nourishes it, and produces "some thirtyfold, some sixty, and some a hundred" (4:20). Scholars debate what an ordinary harvest was in that region, but they agree that yields like these would have astonished Jesus' hearers. Christians who give Christ everything often produce far out of proportion to their numbers. A young convert in West Africa once brought her missionary a silver coin on Christmas Day, when most of the poor congregation brought vegetables or flowers. The missionary feared she had gotten it dishonestly. She explained that she had sold herself to a neighboring planter as a lifelong servant, so that she could lay the price of her whole life at the feet of her Lord. Christ does not only want our money, our attendance, or our talents. He wants all of us.
blocks.es_reference: 4. Algunos reciben la palabra y dan fruto. La buena tierra es abierta, profunda y no dividida. Recibe la semilla, la nutre y produce "a treinta, a sesenta, y a ciento por uno" (4:20). Los eruditos debaten cuál era una cosecha común en aquella región, pero coinciden en que cosechas así habrían asombrado a los oyentes de Jesús. Los cristianos que le dan todo a Cristo a menudo producen mucho más de lo que su número haría pensar. Una joven convertida en África Occidental llevó una vez a su misionero una moneda de plata el día de Navidad, cuando la mayoría de la pobre congregación traía verduras o flores. El misionero temió que la hubiera conseguido de manera deshonesta. Ella explicó que se había vendido a un hacendado vecino como sierva de por vida, para poder poner a los pies de su Señor el precio de toda su vida. Cristo no quiere solo nuestro dinero, nuestra asistencia o nuestros talentos. Nos quiere a nosotros enteros.

blocks.en: II. The Sower's Side of the Story
blocks.es_reference: II. El lado del sembrador

blocks.en: The emphasis of the parable is on the soils, but it also carries great encouragement for everyone who sows the word. The farmer in the story did not examine each square foot of ground before he threw his seed. He sowed generously, knowing that some would be lost, because he knew some would fall on good ground. We do not control the soil. We are called to sow.
blocks.es_reference: El énfasis de la parábola está en los terrenos, pero también trae gran ánimo para todo el que siembra la palabra. El agricultor de la historia no examinó cada palmo de tierra antes de lanzar su semilla. Sembró con generosidad, sabiendo que alguna se perdería, porque sabía que alguna caería en buena tierra. No controlamos la tierra. Somos llamados a sembrar.

blocks.en: Leigh Richmond, an English pastor, once handed tracts to his fellow coach passengers as they walked up a steep hill to spare the horses. One man angrily twisted his tract and threw it on the ground. "Well, you lost that one," someone said. "Maybe not," Richmond answered. "God will take care of it." The wind carried the tract into a field where some haymakers were working. They smoothed it out and read it together, and when the angry man looked back and saw a whole band of men reading what he had thrown away, he was convicted. He was later converted and became a distributor of tracts himself. "Blessed are you who sow beside all waters" (Isaiah 32:20).
blocks.es_reference: Leigh Richmond, un pastor inglés, repartió una vez folletos a sus compañeros de viaje mientras subían a pie una cuesta empinada para aliviar a los caballos. Un hombre torció su folleto con enojo y lo tiró al suelo. "Bueno, ese se perdió", dijo alguien. "Tal vez no", respondió Richmond. "Dios se encargará de él." El viento llevó el folleto a un campo donde trabajaban unos segadores. Lo alisaron y lo leyeron juntos, y cuando el hombre enojado miró atrás y vio a todo un grupo de hombres leyendo lo que él había tirado, fue convencido de pecado. Después se convirtió y llegó a repartir folletos él mismo. "Dichosos vosotros los que sembráis junto a todas las aguas" (Isaías 32:20).

blocks.en: God can use the humblest sower. John R. Rice, who later preached for more than fifty years and wrote many books, told of an evening when he was teaching college and went to help at the Pacific Garden Mission in Chicago. The preacher that night was Holland Oates, a stonemason with a fifth-grade education who had once drunk and cursed with his workers until God saved him. Oates told how, one day after smashing his toe with a stone, he shut his office door and prayed, "Lord, is there anything else You want? If You want me, You can have me. If You want me to sell this business, I'll go to preaching." When he unlocked the door, a man walked in and asked if he would sell his stoneyard. He sold it in half an hour for half its worth. Oates bought a small truck, put a set of chimes and a little organ in it, got a cornet for his son, and went out to the street corners of Chicago. When a crowd gathered, he told them as best he could how to be saved and handed out little mirrors. One side said, "Want to see a sinner? See the other side." As Oates quoted Isaiah's "Here am I; send me," the college teacher's heart was stirred. He too said, "Lord, send me," and that night he led a drunken man to Christ. He said, "Lord, college teaching never was like this!" The stonemason sowed the seed, and God gave fruit that went on for half a century.
blocks.es_reference: Dios puede usar al sembrador más humilde. John R. Rice, que después predicó más de cincuenta años y escribió muchos libros, contó de una noche en que era profesor universitario y fue a ayudar a la Misión Pacific Garden de Chicago. El predicador esa noche era Holland Oates, un cantero con quinto año de primaria que antes bebía y maldecía con sus trabajadores hasta que Dios lo salvó. Oates contó cómo, un día después de aplastarse un dedo del pie con una piedra, cerró la puerta de su oficina y oró: "Señor, ¿hay algo más que quieras? Si me quieres, aquí me tienes. Si quieres que venda este negocio, me iré a predicar." Cuando abrió la puerta, entró un hombre y le preguntó si vendería su cantera. La vendió en media hora por la mitad de su valor. Oates compró una camioneta, le puso unas campanas y un pequeño órgano, consiguió una corneta para su hijo y salió a las esquinas de Chicago. Cuando se reunía la gente, les decía lo mejor que podía cómo ser salvos y repartía pequeños espejos. Un lado decía: "¿Quiere ver a un pecador? Mire el otro lado." Mientras Oates citaba el "Heme aquí, envíame a mí" de Isaías, el corazón del profesor se conmovió. Él también dijo: "Señor, envíame", y esa noche guió a Cristo a un hombre borracho. Dijo: "¡Señor, enseñar en la universidad nunca fue así!" El cantero sembró la semilla, y Dios dio fruto que duró medio siglo.

blocks.en: III. The Lamp and the Measure (Mark 4:21–25)
blocks.es_reference: III. La lámpara y la medida (Marcos 4:21–25)

blocks.en: Right after explaining the sower, Jesus added two short sayings. "Is a lamp brought to be put under a basket or under a bed? Is it not to be set on a lampstand? For there is nothing hidden which will not be revealed" (4:21–22). In Unit 1 we saw that parables both reveal and conceal. Here Jesus makes clear that the concealing is temporary. The light of the kingdom was not given to be hidden. What He whispered to the disciples would one day be proclaimed to the whole world, and those who receive the word are to let it shine.
blocks.es_reference: Justo después de explicar al sembrador, Jesús añadió dos dichos breves. "¿Acaso se trae la luz para ponerla debajo del almud, o debajo de la cama? ¿No es para ponerla en el candelero? Porque no hay nada oculto que no haya de ser manifestado" (4:21–22). En la Unidad 1 vimos que las parábolas revelan y también ocultan. Aquí Jesús deja claro que el ocultar es temporal. La luz del reino no se dio para esconderla. Lo que Él susurró a los discípulos un día sería proclamado al mundo entero, y los que reciben la palabra deben dejarla brillar.

blocks.en: Then He said, "Take heed what you hear. With the same measure you use, it will be measured to you; and to you who hear, more will be given. For whoever has, to him more will be given; but whoever does not have, even what he has will be taken away from him" (4:24–25). This is the parable of the soils put into a proverb. Hearing is never neutral. The one who receives the word with an open heart finds that understanding grows; the one who shuts it out finds that even what little he had slips away. The hard path grows harder, and the good soil grows richer. Every sermon we hear either softens us or hardens us.
blocks.es_reference: Luego dijo: "Mirad lo que oís; porque con la medida con que medís, os será medido, y aun se os añadirá a vosotros los que oís. Porque al que tiene, se le dará; y al que no tiene, aun lo que tiene se le quitará" (4:24–25). Esta es la parábola de los terrenos convertida en proverbio. El oír nunca es neutral. El que recibe la palabra con un corazón abierto descubre que su entendimiento crece; el que la rechaza descubre que aun lo poco que tenía se le escapa. El camino duro se endurece más, y la buena tierra se enriquece más. Cada sermón que oímos nos ablanda o nos endurece.

blocks.en: IV. The Seed That Grows by Itself (Mark 4:26–29)
blocks.es_reference: IV. La semilla que crece por sí sola (Marcos 4:26–29)

blocks.en: Only Mark records this little parable. "The kingdom of God is as if a man should scatter seed on the ground, and should sleep by night and rise by day, and the seed should sprout and grow, he himself does not know how. For the earth yields crops by itself: first the blade, then the head, after that the full grain in the head. But when the grain ripens, immediately he puts in the sickle, because the harvest has come" (4:26–29).
blocks.es_reference: Solo Marcos registra esta pequeña parábola. "Así es el reino de Dios, como cuando un hombre echa semilla en la tierra; y duerme y se levanta, de noche y de día, y la semilla brota y crece sin que él sepa cómo. Porque de suyo lleva fruto la tierra, primero hierba, luego espiga, después grano lleno en la espiga; y cuando el fruto está maduro, en seguida se mete la hoz, porque la siega ha llegado" (4:26–29).

blocks.en: The farmer does his part: he scatters the seed. Then he goes to bed. He cannot make the seed grow by worrying over it, and he does not understand how it grows. The Greek words translated "by itself" give us our word automatic. The growth comes from the life God has put in the seed and the soil. Paul said the same thing about ministry: "I planted, Apollos watered, but God gave the increase. So then neither he who plants is anything, nor he who waters, but God who gives the increase" (1 Corinthians 3:6–7).
blocks.es_reference: El agricultor hace su parte: echa la semilla. Luego se va a dormir. No puede hacer crecer la semilla preocupándose por ella, y no entiende cómo crece. La palabra griega traducida "de suyo" nos da nuestra palabra automático. El crecimiento viene de la vida que Dios ha puesto en la semilla y en la tierra. Pablo dijo lo mismo del ministerio: "Yo planté, Apolos regó; pero el crecimiento lo ha dado Dios. Así que ni el que planta es algo, ni el que riega, sino Dios, que da el crecimiento" (1 Corintios 3:6–7).

blocks.en: This is a word of rest for anxious pastors. We cannot argue anyone into the kingdom, and we cannot force spiritual growth on our timetable. Growth also comes in stages, "first the blade, then the head, after that the full grain." A new believer is not yet a mature one, and we should not expect a full head of grain from a blade that sprouted last week. But the parable also looks to the end: when the grain is ripe, the sickle comes. The quiet, hidden growth of the kingdom is moving toward a harvest. The sower's job is to sow faithfully, sleep peacefully, and trust God with the growth.
blocks.es_reference: Esta es una palabra de descanso para los pastores ansiosos. No podemos convencer a nadie a fuerza de argumentos para que entre al reino, ni podemos forzar el crecimiento espiritual según nuestro calendario. El crecimiento también viene por etapas, "primero hierba, luego espiga, después grano lleno en la espiga". Un nuevo creyente todavía no es un creyente maduro, y no debemos esperar una espiga llena de una hierba que brotó la semana pasada. Pero la parábola también mira al final: cuando el fruto está maduro, viene la hoz. El crecimiento callado y escondido del reino avanza hacia una siega. La tarea del sembrador es sembrar con fidelidad, dormir en paz y confiar a Dios el crecimiento.

blocks.en: V. Preaching the Sower
blocks.es_reference: V. Cómo predicar al sembrador

blocks.en: The parable of the soils preaches well with four points: some people refuse to hear, some have a shallow response, some have divided hearts, and some bear fruit. Each point needs a clear picture of the soil and a clear picture of the person. Close by asking listeners which soil describes them today, and invite them to receive the word into good, deep, undivided ground. A second sermon can speak to the sowers in the congregation: sow generously, like the farmer; sow faithfully, like Holland Oates; and rest in God's power to give the growth, like the man who slept while the seed grew. Remember Jesus' own warning, "Take heed what you hear," and remember that it applies to the preacher first.
blocks.es_reference: La parábola de los terrenos se predica bien con cuatro puntos: algunos se niegan a oír, algunos tienen una respuesta superficial, algunos tienen el corazón dividido y algunos dan fruto. Cada punto necesita un cuadro claro del terreno y un cuadro claro de la persona. Concluya preguntando a los oyentes qué terreno los describe hoy, e invítelos a recibir la palabra en tierra buena, profunda y no dividida. Un segundo sermón puede hablar a los sembradores de la congregación: siembre con generosidad, como el agricultor; siembre con fidelidad, como Holland Oates; y descanse en el poder de Dios para dar el crecimiento, como el hombre que dormía mientras la semilla crecía. Recuerde la advertencia de Jesús, "Mirad lo que oís", y recuerde que se aplica primero al predicador.

blocks.en: Closing
blocks.es_reference: Conclusión

blocks.en: Jesus ended the parable of the sower with a call: "He who has ears to hear, let him hear!" (Mark 4:9). The seed is good, and the Sower is faithful. The question is the soil. Will we let the word stay on the surface, spring up and wither, or be choked by other loves? Or will we receive it into good, deep, undivided ground, and give Christ everything? He does not want only part of us. He wants all of us.
blocks.es_reference: Jesús terminó la parábola del sembrador con un llamado: "El que tiene oídos para oír, oiga" (Marcos 4:9). La semilla es buena, y el Sembrador es fiel. La pregunta es la tierra. ¿Dejaremos que la palabra se quede en la superficie, brote y se seque, o sea ahogada por otros amores? ¿O la recibiremos en tierra buena, profunda y no dividida, y le daremos todo a Cristo? Él no quiere solo una parte de nosotros. Nos quiere enteros.

blocks.en:
— Dr. Wayne Cook
Chapala Theological Seminary

mc.why: "The sower sows the word" (Mark 4:14).

mc.stem: Why did the seed on the path fail to grow?
options: The path was packed as hard as cement, and birds took the seed
mc.why: It pictures those who refuse to hear; Satan takes the word away (Mark 4:15).

mc.stem: The rocky ground in the parable was:
options: A field full of loose stones
A thin layer of soil over a shelf of limestone
mc.why: The seed sprang up quickly but had no depth of root and withered in the sun.

mc.stem: The story of the seminary student who began with "Yeah, okay" teaches that:
options: The size of the first response does not predict the depth of the root
mc.why: Many excited converts fell away, but the quiet young man's mustard seed of faith grew.

mc.stem: According to this unit, Paul's response on the Damascus road shows that:
options: Enthusiasm is a poor substitute for faith
mc.why: Paul spent three days in blindness, prayer, and fasting, considering what had happened (Acts 9:9).

mc.stem: The thorny ground pictures people whose hearts are:
options: Divided, with cares and riches choking the word
mc.why: Like the rich young ruler, they want Christ but love other things more (Mark 4:19).

mc.stem: The young convert in West Africa showed the fruit of good soil by:
options: Selling herself as a lifelong servant to give a coin to her Lord
mc.why: Christ does not want only our money or time; He wants all of us.

mc.stem: The Leigh Richmond tract story encourages the sower because:
options: The angry man threw the tract in a river
God cared for the seed that seemed lost and brought fruit
mc.why: "Blessed are you who sow beside all waters" (Isaiah 32:20).

mc.stem: Jesus said, "Do you not understand this parable? How then will you understand all the parables?" This suggests the parable of the sower:
options: Teaches us how to hear every other parable
mc.why: The sower is a parable about hearing itself (Mark 4:13).

mc.stem: Holland Oates, the stonemason-preacher, shows that:
options: God can use the humblest sower to produce lasting fruit
mc.why: His preaching stirred a college teacher, John R. Rice, who preached for more than fifty years.

mc.stem: Holland Oates's little mirrors said:
options: "Want to see a sinner? See the other side."
mc.why: The other side was the mirror, showing the reader himself.

mc.stem: In the saying about the lamp (Mark 4:21–22), Jesus teaches that:
options: The concealing of the parables is temporary; the light is meant to shine
Lamps should be kept under beds
The kingdom must stay secret forever
mc.why: There is nothing hidden which will not be revealed.

mc.stem: "Take heed what you hear... whoever has, to him more will be given" means that:
options: Hearing is never neutral; open hearts grow in understanding and closed hearts lose even what they had
mc.why: It is the parable of the soils put into a proverb: every sermon softens us or hardens us.

mc.stem: The parable of the seed that grows by itself is found only in:
mc.why: Mark 4:26–29 is unique to Mark's Gospel.

mc.stem: The Greek words translated "by itself" in Mark 4:28 give us the English word:
mc.why: The growth comes from the life God has placed in the seed and soil.

mc.stem: Paul's words "I planted, Apollos watered, but God gave the increase" support the lesson that:
options: Ministers make the church grow by their own power
We sow faithfully, but God gives the growth
mc.why: The farmer sleeps and rises while the seed grows, he himself does not know how.

mc.stem: "First the blade, then the head, after that the full grain" reminds us that:
options: Spiritual growth comes in stages, so new believers need patience
mc.why: We should not expect a full head of grain from a blade that sprouted last week.

mc.stem: A second sermon on Mark 4 for the sowers in a congregation might urge them to:
options: Examine each person before sharing the gospel
Stop sowing when some seed is lost
Sow generously, sow faithfully, and rest in God's power to give growth
mc.why: Like the farmer, Holland Oates, and the man who slept while the seed grew.

mc.stem: In Mark 4:1, Jesus taught the crowd while:
options: Sitting in a boat on the Sea of Galilee
mc.why: The whole multitude stood on the shore, with farm fields on the hillsides behind them.

sa.prompt: Describe the path and the rocky ground in the parable of the sower and what each pictures.
sa.model: The path between the narrow fields was trampled hard as cement, so seed could not penetrate and birds took it. It pictures people who refuse to hear, whether indifferent or hardened, as Satan takes the word away. The rocky ground was a thin layer of soil over limestone; seed sprang up but had no root and withered. It pictures a shallow response, like foxhole conversions that do not last.

sa.prompt: Contrast enthusiasm and faith using the alcoholic gambler, Paul, and the seminary student.
sa.model: The young alcoholic gambler had a religious experience when his wife was leaving, but the first trouble destroyed it; he substituted enthusiasm for faith. Paul did not jump for joy on the Damascus road but spent three days in blindness, prayer, and fasting. The seminary student began quietly with "Yeah, okay," while excited converts fell away, yet his mustard seed of faith grew. Enthusiasm is a poor substitute for faith.

sa.prompt: Explain the thorny ground and the good soil, including the West African convert.
sa.model: The thorny ground looked clean because the weeds had been cut and burned, but the roots remained and choked the wheat. It pictures divided hearts where cares, riches, and other desires choke the word, like the rich young ruler. The good soil is open, deep, and undivided, bearing thirtyfold, sixty, and a hundred. The West African convert sold herself as a lifelong servant to give a coin to Christ; He wants all of us.

sa.prompt: Explain how the parable of the sower encourages those who sow the word, using the Leigh Richmond story.
sa.model: We do not control the soil; we are called to sow. Leigh Richmond gave tracts to fellow coach passengers, and one angry man twisted his and threw it down. Richmond said God would take care of it. The wind carried it to haymakers who smoothed it out and read it, and seeing them, the angry man was convicted and later converted. Blessed are those who sow beside all waters.

sa.prompt: Explain why Mark 4:13 suggests the parable of the sower is a key to all the parables, and describe the setting in Mark 4:1.
sa.model: Jesus asked, "Do you not understand this parable? How then will you understand all the parables?" The sower is about hearing itself, so it teaches us how to hear every other parable. So many people gathered by the Sea of Galilee that Jesus sat in a boat while the crowd stood on the shore, with fields visible on the hillsides. He began, "Listen! Behold, a sower went out to sow."

sa.prompt: Tell the story of Holland Oates and John R. Rice and explain what it teaches sowers.
sa.model: Holland Oates was a stonemason with a fifth-grade education whom God saved. He offered himself to God, sold his stoneyard in half an hour, and preached on Chicago street corners from a truck with chimes and an organ, handing out mirrors that said, "Want to see a sinner? See the other side." Hearing him at the Pacific Garden Mission, college teacher John R. Rice said, "Lord, send me," and preached for more than fifty years. God can use the humblest sower to bring lasting fruit.

sa.prompt: Explain the sayings about the lamp and the measure in Mark 4:21–25.
sa.model: A lamp is not put under a basket but on a lampstand, and nothing hidden will stay hidden; the concealing of the parables is temporary and the light is meant to shine. Jesus also said, "Take heed what you hear," for with the measure you use it will be measured to you: to whoever has, more will be given, and from whoever does not have, even what he has will be taken away. Hearing is never neutral; each sermon softens or hardens us.

sa.prompt: Explain the parable of the seed that grows by itself and its encouragement for pastors.
sa.model: A man scatters seed, then sleeps and rises while it sprouts and grows, he himself does not know how, for the earth yields crops by itself, a phrase that gives us the word automatic. Paul said he planted and Apollos watered, but God gave the increase. Pastors cannot force growth; it comes in stages, first the blade, then the head, then the full grain. When the grain is ripe the sickle comes. We sow faithfully, sleep peacefully, and trust God with the growth.

sa.prompt: Outline two sermons from Mark 4: one on the soils and one for the sowers.
sa.model: The first sermon has four points: some refuse to hear, some have a shallow response, some have divided hearts, and some bear fruit, each with a clear picture of the soil and the person, closing by asking which soil describes the listener. The second speaks to sowers: sow generously like the farmer, sow faithfully like Holland Oates, and rest in God's power to give the growth like the man who slept while the seed grew. The warning "Take heed what you hear" applies to the preacher first.

sa.prompt: Match each of the four soils to Jesus' own explanation in Mark 4:14–20.
sa.model: The seed by the wayside pictures those from whom Satan immediately takes away the word. The stony ground pictures those who receive it with gladness but have no root and stumble when tribulation or persecution comes. The thorns picture those in whom the cares of this world, the deceitfulness of riches, and other desires choke the word. The good ground pictures those who hear, accept it, and bear fruit thirty, sixty, and a hundredfold.
